notes: Built from publicly documented FACE-Q Craniofacial Module scale names (with Aesthetics/Skin Cancer scales where they apply) and what those scales measure. Descriptions are paraphrased constructs; no questionnaire item text is included. Conversations may be with the child (self), a guardian speaking about the child (guardian), or both; drill-down cues address the guardian view where useful. For satisfaction-type constructs, 'severity' expresses the degree of dissatisfaction or concern. Constructs with 'applicable_timepoints' are only active at those timepoints (extension to SPEC §6, see seed/README.md). Construct ids are shared with face-q-adult where the construct is the same so diagnosis focus lists work across both maps.

constructs.label: How the child feels about their face overall
constructs.description: How the child feels about their face as a whole: in the mirror, in school photos, on video, and compared with friends and siblings. If the guardian answers: what the child says and shows about their face.

severity_signals.none: happy with or unbothered by their face
severity_signals.mild: sometimes mentions something they would change; no avoidance
severity_signals.moderate: often unhappy about their face; avoids photos or mirrors sometimes
severity_signals.severe: very upset about their face; avoidance or upset that affects school or play

drill_down: Which part of the face bothers them most
Teasing or comments from other children
Whether they avoid photos, mirrors or activities
What the child hopes will change
Whether the guardian's view matches the child's

constructs.label: How the child feels about their nose
constructs.description: How the child feels about the shape and size of their nose and nostrils, from the front and the side, and whether it looks like other children's.

severity_signals.mild: occasionally mentions it
severity_signals.moderate: often bothered; notices it in photos or when others look
severity_signals.severe: nose is a constant worry; hides it or gets very upset about it

drill_down: Nostril shape, tip, width or profile
Whether other children comment
Whether breathing is also a problem

constructs.label: How the child feels about their eyes
constructs.description: How the child feels about the look of their eyes and eyelids, including whether they look even and whether other children notice.

severity_signals.mild: sometimes notices a difference
severity_signals.moderate: often bothered; unevenness or shape is a regular worry
severity_signals.severe: eyes are a major source of upset; hides them or avoids being looked at

drill_down: Shape, position, eyelids or evenness
Whether glasses or patches are involved and how they feel about them
Whether vision is affected

constructs.label: How the child feels about their lips
constructs.description: How the child feels about the shape, evenness and look of their lips and the area above the lip, including any cleft-related differences.

severity_signals.mild: sometimes notices a difference
severity_signals.moderate: often bothered; covers their mouth or avoids smiling in photos
severity_signals.severe: lips are a constant worry; strongly avoids smiling or being looked at

drill_down: Shape, evenness or the area above the lip
Whether they cover their mouth when smiling or laughing
Whether other children ask about it

constructs.label: How the child feels about their ears
constructs.description: How the child feels about the size, shape, position and evenness of their ears, including whether they hide them with hair or hats.

severity_signals.mild: sometimes notices; no hiding
severity_signals.moderate: often bothered; hides ears with hair or hats
severity_signals.severe: ears are a major upset; refuses haircuts, swimming or activities that expose them

drill_down: Size, shape, position or one side versus the other
Whether they hide their ears (hair, hats)
Whether hearing aids or hearing are part of it
Whether other children comment

constructs.label: How the child feels about their cheeks and mid-face
constructs.description: How the child feels about the shape and evenness of their cheeks and the middle part of the face, including whether one side looks different.

severity_signals.mild: sometimes notices flatness or unevenness
severity_signals.moderate: often bothered by unevenness
severity_signals.severe: cheek appearance is a major upset; avoids photos or certain angles

drill_down: Whether one side looks different
Whether it is more noticeable when smiling
Whether it has changed with growth or treatment

constructs.label: How the child feels about their chin and jaw
constructs.description: How the child feels about the size, shape and position of their chin and jaw, including whether the jaw looks uneven or set back.

severity_signals.mild: sometimes notices
severity_signals.moderate: often bothered; unevenness or profile is a regular worry
severity_signals.severe: chin or jaw is a major upset; avoids side views or photos

drill_down: Chin size, jaw evenness or profile
Whether chewing or bite is also affected
Whether it has changed with growth

constructs.label: How the child feels about their smile and teeth
constructs.description: How the child feels about their smile and teeth: whether the smile looks even and natural, and whether teeth, gums or the lip line make them hold back from smiling.

severity_signals.mild: sometimes self-conscious about smiling
severity_signals.moderate: often holds back or covers their smile
severity_signals.severe: avoids smiling or laughing in front of others

drill_down: Teeth, gums, evenness or lip movement
Whether they cover their mouth when laughing
Whether braces or dental treatment are involved
Whether it matters more in photos or with friends

constructs.label: How the child feels about the skin on their face
constructs.description: How the child feels about the colour, texture and evenness of the skin on their face, including birthmarks, patches or changes after treatment.

severity_signals.mild: sometimes notices
severity_signals.moderate: often bothered; wants to cover it
severity_signals.severe: skin is a major upset; avoids being seen without covering it

drill_down: Colour, patches, texture or marks
Whether other children ask about it
Whether they try to cover it

constructs.label: Confidence and feeling good about oneself
constructs.description: How sure of themselves the child feels around other children and adults, whether they feel 'like everyone else', and whether their face makes them feel different or less good about themselves. Guardian view: how the child's confidence shows at home and out and about.

severity_signals.none: confident; feels like the other kids
severity_signals.mild: confidence dips in some situations (new people, performances)
severity_signals.moderate: often lacks confidence because of their face; hangs back
severity_signals.severe: very low confidence; says or shows they feel different or not good enough most of the time

drill_down: Situations where confidence drops (new class, sports, performances)
Activities where they feel good about themselves
Whether the guardian has noticed a change over the past months
Whether the child says they feel different from other children

constructs.label: Accepting how they look
constructs.description: Whether the child accepts their face as part of who they are, or often wishes they looked different; how they talk about their face when it comes up.

severity_signals.none: accepts their face; talks about it matter-of-factly
severity_signals.mild: mostly accepting; occasional wishes to look different
severity_signals.moderate: often wishes they looked different; upset when it comes up
severity_signals.severe: cannot accept how they look; strong sense of being defined by their face

drill_down: How the child explains their face to others
Whether they ask why they look different
What helps them feel okay about it

constructs.label: Sadness, worry or anger about their face
constructs.description: Whether the child seems sad, worried, frustrated or angry because of their face or its treatment; how often, and how the guardian sees it affecting them at home (sleep, tears, withdrawal, anger).

severity_signals.none: mood not affected by their face
severity_signals.mild: occasional bad days linked to their face or appointments
severity_signals.moderate: regular sadness or worry about their face; recovers with comfort or distraction
severity_signals.severe: persistent sadness, worry or anger affecting sleep, appetite, school or play

drill_down: Signs the guardian notices (withdrawal, tears, anger, sleep)
Whether it is worse around school events, photos or hospital visits
Whether the child has talked to anyone about it
Whether treatment has changed this

constructs.label: Comfort with friends and in play
constructs.description: How comfortable the child is with friends, at parties, in group play and sport, and meeting new children; whether they join in or hang back.

severity_signals.none: joins in freely; has friends they feel relaxed with
severity_signals.mild: slightly shy with new children; fine with friends
severity_signals.moderate: often hangs back; prefers one or two familiar friends or adults
severity_signals.severe: very uncomfortable with other children; isolated or refuses group activities

drill_down: Whether they have close friends
Whether they join in at break time, parties, sport
Whether new settings (new class, clubs) are hard
What helps them feel comfortable

constructs.label: School participation
constructs.description: How the child is doing at school: attendance, taking part in class and activities, concentration, and whether their face, its treatment or other children's reactions get in the way.

severity_signals.mild: occasional reluctance (class photos, presentations)
severity_signals.moderate: regularly avoids some school activities or misses days because of their face or treatment
severity_signals.severe: school refusal, frequent absence or major withdrawal linked to their face

drill_down: Days missed and why
Activities they avoid (speaking in class, sport, photos)
Whether the school knows and helps
Whether schoolwork or concentration is affected

constructs.label: Teasing, staring and questions from others
constructs.description: Whether the child is teased, stared at, asked questions or left out at school or in play because of their face; how they respond and whether they tell the guardian.

severity_signals.none: no teasing or comments that bother them
severity_signals.mild: occasional questions or looks they handle well
severity_signals.moderate: regular comments or teasing that upset them or that they plan around
severity_signals.severe: bullying or exclusion; significant hurt, fear or avoidance of school

drill_down: Who it comes from and where it happens
Whether the child tells the guardian or a teacher
Whether the school knows and what they have done
Whether the child has a comeback or plan for questions

constructs.label: Avoiding activities because of their face
constructs.description: Whether the child avoids photos, parties, swimming, sport, performances or meeting new people because of how their face looks or works.

severity_signals.mild: occasionally opts out of photos or new activities
severity_signals.moderate: regularly avoids some activities because of their face
severity_signals.severe: withdrawn from most activities outside home

drill_down: Specific activities skipped recently
How often in the last month
Whether the guardian has changed family plans because of it

constructs.label: Worrying about or checking their face
constructs.description: How often the child talks about, checks, or worries about their face; whether they compare themselves with others; whether the guardian sees this taking up a lot of the child's attention.

severity_signals.none: rarely mentions or thinks about it
severity_signals.mild: brings it up now and then; easily reassured
severity_signals.moderate: brings it up most days; checks mirrors or photos; needs reassurance
severity_signals.severe: constant worry or checking that is hard to interrupt; upset when reassured

drill_down: How often it comes up in a typical week
Mirror or photo checking, comparing with others
Whether it affects sleep or concentration
When it started or got worse

constructs.label: Hiding their face or a feature
constructs.description: Whether the child tries to hide their face or a feature: hair over the face or ears, hats, hands over the mouth, turning away in photos, or refusing haircuts or swimming.

severity_signals.mild: hides sometimes (photos, new people)
severity_signals.moderate: hides most days; upset if they cannot
severity_signals.severe: will not be seen without hiding; refuses activities that would expose the feature

drill_down: What they hide and how
Whether it affects haircuts, swimming, sport or uniform rules
How they react if they cannot hide

constructs.label: Breathing through the nose
constructs.description: Whether the child breathes easily through their nose during the day, during play or sport, and at night; mouth breathing, snoring or disturbed sleep.

severity_signals.mild: occasional blockage (colds, one side, at night)
severity_signals.moderate: regularly mouth-breathes, snores or tires during play
severity_signals.severe: constant obstruction; poor sleep, restless nights or limits on activity

drill_down: One side or both; day or night
Snoring, restless sleep or tiredness
Whether it limits running or sport
Whether it changed after surgery

constructs.label: Eating and drinking
constructs.description: Whether the child can bite, chew, keep food and drink in the mouth, eat a normal range of foods, and eat comfortably at school or with others; food or liquid coming out of the nose.

severity_signals.mild: avoids a few foods or is a slow eater
severity_signals.moderate: regular difficulty chewing, spilling or leaking; avoids eating in front of others
severity_signals.severe: eating is a daily struggle; growth, nutrition or school meals significantly affected

drill_down: Which foods or textures are hard
Spilling, leaking or food coming through the nose
Whether they avoid eating at school or with friends
Growth or weight concerns

constructs.label: Speaking and being understood
constructs.description: How clearly the child speaks, whether strangers, teachers and other children understand them, whether speech sounds nasal, and whether they hold back from talking because of it.

severity_signals.mild: occasionally asked to repeat; a few sounds are harder
severity_signals.moderate: regularly not understood by people outside the family; holds back in class
severity_signals.severe: speech seriously limits communication at school; relies on family to interpret

drill_down: Which sounds or situations are hardest
Whether teachers or other children understand them
Whether they avoid speaking up or reading aloud
Speech therapy and progress

constructs.label: Facial expression and movement
constructs.description: Whether the child can smile, frown, raise their eyebrows, close their eyes and show feelings with their face; whether expressions look even and whether others misread them.

severity_signals.mild: slight unevenness the family notices
severity_signals.moderate: expressions look uneven or limited; others misread their mood
severity_signals.severe: cannot show feelings with the face; eye closure or lip problems

drill_down: Which movements are affected
Whether others misread their expression
Eye closure, dryness or drooling
Whether it is improving, stable or worsening

constructs.label: Pain or discomfort
constructs.description: Whether the child says it hurts or shows signs of pain (rubbing, crying, not wanting to be touched, not eating) in the face or treated area; how constant it is and what it stops them doing.

severity_signals.mild: occasional mild discomfort; no pain relief needed
severity_signals.moderate: regular pain needing pain relief or limiting play or eating
severity_signals.severe: constant or severe pain affecting sleep, eating or daily function

drill_down: Where it hurts and how the child shows it
What makes it better or worse
Pain relief used and whether it helps
Whether it is improving

constructs.label: Swelling, bruising and redness
constructs.description: Swelling, bruising, redness or lumpiness in the treated area; how visible it is and whether it is settling as the family was told to expect.

severity_signals.mild: slight swelling only the family notices
severity_signals.moderate: visible swelling or bruising that other children comment on
severity_signals.severe: marked swelling affecting eating, breathing or vision, or keeping the child home

drill_down: Which areas and whether it is one-sided
Trend since treatment
Whether it affects eating, breathing or vision
What the family was told to expect

constructs.label: Numbness, tingling or itching
constructs.description: Numb, tingly, itchy or strange feelings in the face or treated area; whether the child mentions it or touches or picks at the area.

severity_signals.mild: small numb patch rarely mentioned
severity_signals.moderate: noticeable numbness or itching that bothers the child daily
severity_signals.severe: widespread or painful altered sensation affecting eating or comfort

drill_down: Location and extent
Whether it is changing over time
Whether it affects eating or drinking

constructs.label: Scars
constructs.description: How the child and guardian feel about the child's scars (for example a cleft lip scar or surgical scars): visibility, colour, texture, and whether other children notice or ask.

severity_signals.none: scars not noticeable or not a concern
severity_signals.mild: notices the scar but it does not bother them much
severity_signals.moderate: scar is visible and bothers the child; some hiding; other children ask
severity_signals.severe: scar dominates how the child sees their face; significant upset or avoidance

drill_down: Which scars and where
Colour, texture or raised areas
Whether other children ask about the scar
Whether the child wants to hide it
Scar care being used

constructs.label: Unevenness or asymmetry
constructs.description: Whether the child or guardian sees one side of the face or a feature as different from the other, and how much this bothers the child.

severity_signals.mild: slight unevenness only the family notices
severity_signals.moderate: unevenness seen in most photos; other children may notice
severity_signals.severe: asymmetry is highly visible to the child; strong upset or avoidance

drill_down: Which feature or side
Whether it is worse when smiling or talking
Whether it has changed with growth or treatment

constructs.label: Getting back to school, play and normal routines
constructs.description: In the weeks after treatment: whether the child is back to school, play, sport, normal eating and sleep; how much help they need; and how the family is managing care and time off.

severity_signals.mild: minor limits (e.g., no contact sport yet)
severity_signals.moderate: missing school or regular activities; needs help with some tasks; family routines disrupted
severity_signals.severe: largely at home or dependent on carers; recovery much harder than the family expected

drill_down: Days of school missed
Whether they can play and sleep as usual
How the family is coping with care and time off
Whether recovery matches what the family was told

domains.label: Satisfaction with outcome, decision and information

constructs.label: Satisfaction with the result
constructs.description: After treatment: whether the child and guardian are pleased with the result, whether it looks the way they hoped and natural, and whether they feel it was worth it.

severity_signals.none: pleased; result met or exceeded hopes
severity_signals.mild: mostly pleased with a small reservation
severity_signals.moderate: mixed; clear disappointment in one or more aspects
severity_signals.severe: regret, or the child or guardian feel things are worse than before

drill_down: What the child says about the change
Whether the guardian's hopes were met
Which aspect disappoints, if any
Whether their view is shifting as healing progresses

constructs.label: Satisfaction with the decision to have treatment
constructs.description: Whether the guardian (and child, where old enough) feel the decision to have treatment, and its timing, was right for the child and made with enough information and time.

severity_signals.none: confident the decision and timing were right
severity_signals.mild: small doubts but glad overall
severity_signals.moderate: meaningful second thoughts about the decision or its timing
severity_signals.severe: regrets the decision or felt pressured

drill_down: What influenced the decision
Whether the child was involved and how they felt about it
Whether they felt rushed or pressured

constructs.label: Satisfaction with information received
constructs.description: Whether the family felt well informed before and after treatment about what to expect, recovery, risks and care at home, and whether the child had things explained at their level.

severity_signals.mild: a few things they wish they had been told
severity_signals.moderate: important gaps; surprised by parts of recovery or result
severity_signals.severe: felt uninformed or misled; major unexpected consequences

drill_down: What the family wishes they had known
Whether the child had things explained at their level
Questions they still have for the team
